latest_release.name: 2026.48.0 (alpha)
latest_release.body:
Ladybird 2026.48.0 can unload background tabs to save memory, lets you choose which tabs share a process, shows what sites are playing in the macOS Now Playing controls, adds AppImage packages for Linux, and makes scrolling and XML parsing faster.

Ladybird updates itself on macOS and through the package manager on Linux, or you can download it from https://ladybird.org/download/.

## New features

- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15199: Ladybird can now unload background tabs to save memory. It does this when the system runs low on memory, and also for tabs that have been hidden for two hours. Tabs you typed into, tabs that are downloading and tabs waiting for an answer stay loaded. A new Memory section in the settings lets you change the time or turn the timer off. Unloaded tabs show a faded icon in the tab strip, and the task manager shows which tabs can be unloaded.
- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15212: A new setting lets you choose whether tabs share a process never, by origin (as before) or by site. Sharing uses less memory, but a crash in one tab then also closes the tabs that share its process.
- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/14595: Added the Media Session API. On macOS, media that pages play now shows in the system's Now Playing controls, with title, artwork and position, and those controls and the media keys work.
- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15128: Pages now follow the system's reduced motion and contrast settings on macOS and Linux, through `prefers-reduced-motion` and the contrast preference.
- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15227: You can now choose to trust self-signed certificates.
- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15724: Added Qwant as a search engine, with search suggestions.
- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15436: Videos in RGB and grayscale formats now play, and VideoToolbox can now output 4:2:2 video on macOS.

## Web compatibility

- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15190, https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15355: `<embed>` elements now load HTML documents and images. `<object>` elements show their fallback content when they have no data, and now render inside shadow trees.
- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/14906: Clicks are now `PointerEvent`s, so clicking the video or the progress bar of embedded YouTube players works. MP4 files whose track handler name is not valid UTF-8 now play.
- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15222: The Service Worker API is hidden until service workers can run, so sites such as Telegram Web fall back to paths that work, and their voice messages play.
- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15682, https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15182, https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15172: Added support for these legacy features that sites use:
  - `-webkit-gradient()` and `-webkit-text-security`
  - prefixed `text-align` keywords and `-webkit-device-pixel-ratio` media queries
  - the `lower-latin` and `upper-latin` counter styles
  - quotation marks chosen by the content's language
  - correct sizing of `-webkit-box` items
- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/14991, https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15308: SVG text has many fixes:
  - `textLength`, text decorations, color emoji and `text-transform`
  - `<tspan>` on `<textPath>`, and links inside text
  - correct `dx`/`dy` and `text-anchor` positioning
  - `getStartPositionOfChar()` and `getEndPositionOfChar()`
  - event handler attributes on SVG elements

detail.readme:
# Ladybird

[Ladybird](https://ladybird.org) is a truly independent web browser, using a novel engine based on web standards.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Ladybird is in a pre-alpha state, and only suitable for use by developers
>

## Features

We aim to build a complete, usable browser for the modern web.

Ladybird uses a [multi-process architecture](Documentation/ProcessArchitecture.md) with a main UI process,
WebContent renderer processes, and helper processes for tasks such as networking, image decoding, compositing and media.

Documents from different sites run in separate renderer processes, each sandboxed from the rest of the system.
Image decoding and network connections are done out of process, separately for each site, to be more robust against
malicious content.

At the moment, many core library support components are inherited from SerenityOS:

- LibWeb: Web rendering engine
- LibJS: JavaScript engine
- LibWasm: WebAssembly implementation
- LibCrypto/LibTLS: Cryptography primitives and Transport Layer Security
- LibHTTP: HTTP/1.1 client
- LibGfx: 2D Graphics Library, Image Decoding and Rendering
- LibUnicode: Unicode and locale support
- LibMedia: Audio and video playback
- LibCore: Event loop, OS abstraction layer
- LibIPC: Inter-process communication

## How do I build and run this?

See [build instructions](Documentation/BuildInstructionsLadybird.md) for information on how to build Ladybird.

Ladybird runs on Linux, macOS, Windows (with WSL2), and many other \*Nixes.

## How do I read the documentation?

Code-related documentation can be found in the [documentation](Documentation/) folder.

## Get in touch and participate!

Join [our Discord server](https://discord.gg/nvfjVJ4Svh) to participate in issue and development discussions.

Please read [Getting involved with Ladybird](Documentation/GettingStartedContributing.md) if you're new to Ladybird and want to help.

Before opening an issue, please see the [issue policy](CONTRIBUTING.md#issue-policy) and the [detailed issue-reporting guidelines](ISSUES.md).

The project participation guidelines can be found in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md).
